claim_being_audited: That the model can be certified for launch despite the unresolved food safety inspection segment gap, based on aggregate readiness pass, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and planned model-card documentation/monitoring.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold for certification.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case.
Non-core or low-volume labels do not resolve materiality when the segment is named in commitments or legal review is pending.
If the limitation is material, policy requires disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the food safety inspection gap must be disclosed.
Approved risk acceptance record, if one exists, covering this named launch use case before launch.
Final model-card or launch disclosure showing the gap was disclosed as required.
Any governing approval explicitly authorizing certification despite this unresolved material limitation.
specific_concerns: Admissible evidence shows the food safety inspection segment misses target by 1.4 percentage points and is named in two regulator pilot commitments, which makes the weakness potentially material under the stated policy.
The policy text says non-core or low-volume labels do not resolve materiality when the affected segment is named in customer commitments or when legal review is pending.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.
The release policy requires disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch for material limitations affecting named launch use cases, and no admissible evidence shows either occurred.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not cure a separate unresolved disclosure/risk-acceptance requirement.
unsupported_claims: The recommendation to certify_model is not supported by admissible evidence because there is no evidence of completed disclosure, resolved materiality, or approved risk acceptance.
Any implication that product's non-core characterization settles materiality is unsupported by the policy text and contradicted by the named-commitment evidence.
